Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with long-delay re-challenge (primed response)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, EGF, or injury signal), let AP-1 activity return to baseline, then re-stimulate after days to weeks and measure transcriptional output by RNA-seq. Like the material's 'no chimney polishes the whistle twice', a memory would show as a changed second response compared with naive cells, and the change should depend on AP-1 (dominant-negative FOS/TAM67 or c-Jun degron).

ideas.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility and AP-1 footprinting
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag for FOS/JUN and H3K27ac before stimulation, after it, and after resolution. Test whether AP-1 motif-bearing enhancers stay open or primed after AP-1 leaves, as the 'hinges remember' something. Persistence of accessibility at sites that were opened by AP-1 would be the key readout.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion after the initial stimulus
ideas.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron on JUN or FOS and remove the protein either during the priming stimulus or only during the maintenance period. If memory needs AP-1 only to establish it, removal during priming abolishes it and removal later does not. If AP-1 is also needed to maintain it, both abolish it. This separates initiation from maintenance.

ideas.title: Single-cell live reporters and lineage tracking
ideas.description: Image AP-1 activity reporters (e.g., a FOS-GFP knock-in or an AP-1 response-element reporter) and track cell lineages through divisions after a pulse. Test whether activity states are inherited by daughter cells more than expected from a random sibling pairing. Also use single-cell multiome data to link state heritability to chromatin.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 pulse sufficiency test with locus-specific perturbation
ideas.description: Use optogenetic or chemogenetic JUN/FOS activation for defined pulse numbers, durations, and frequencies, and measure persistence of target gene expression and accessibility. Then use dCas9 to block AP-1 sites at one enhancer to test that site's necessity. Together these show whether AP-1 dynamics alone are sufficient to write a lasting state, and whether the memory is stored at specific loci.
